title: 22yo M - Unhelmeted Motorcycle Crash (ATLS)
chiefComplaint: Brought in by EMS after high-speed motorcycle crash
background: Patient crashed his motorcycle into a pole at high speed. He was not wearing a helmet. EMS reports he smells strongly of alcohol. His right thigh is grossly deformed.

exam.finding: Lethargic, groaning to pain. Right thigh swollen and deformed with a laceration.
Tachycardic, weak pulses, delayed capillary refill.

investigations.name: eFAST Ultrasound
investigations.report: Negative for pericardial effusion. Negative for intraperitoneal free fluid. Bilateral lung sliding present.

start.narrative: A major trauma patient arrives. He is in shock (HR 135, BP 85/40) and has an altered level of consciousness (GCS 8). According to ATLS, what is your FIRST priority?

options.text: C: Circulation - Start Massive Transfusion Protocol

correct_airway.narrative: Airway secured with an endotracheal tube (C-spine protected). SpO2 improves to 100%. However, the patient remains in hypovolemic shock. What is the next step in the Primary Survey?

options.text: B/C: Pelvic binder, Femur Splint, & Massive Transfusion Protocol (MTP)
Push 2 Liters of Normal Saline rapidly

wrong_ct.narrative: Never send an unstable, unprotected airway patient to the CT scanner! The patient aspirates in the scanner and dies from hypoxia.

wrong_splint.narrative: While the femur is broken, ATLS dictates A (Airway) and B (Breathing) come before C (Circulation/Bleeding control). The patient's airway compromises while you are distracted by the leg.

wrong_mtp_first.narrative: Blood is running, but the patient's GCS of 8 means they cannot protect their airway. They begin to aspirate their own vomit.

wrong_fluids.narrative: Current ATLS guidelines advise against large volumes of clear crystalloids (dilutes clotting factors, causes hypothermia). The patient needs blood products (1:1:1 ratio) for hemorrhagic shock.

correct_circulation.narrative: Excellent! Traction splint applied to the femur reducing blood loss, and MTP initiated. Blood pressure stabilizes. The patient is now stable enough for a CT Pan-Scan and Orthopedic consult.
